key_insight: Combining front-surface silicon nanocones with embedded air nanoholes creates a hybrid light-trapping architecture that reduces reflection and boosts absorption in thin-film silicon solar cells.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical route to higher-efficiency, thermally robust thin-film photovoltaics by improving optical confinement without changing the material system.
method: Used FDTD simulations to optimize the nanocone-nanohole geometry for light management.
Coupled optical results with electrical device modeling to predict solar-cell performance.
Evaluated opto-electro-thermal behavior under isothermal and non-isothermal conditions up to 45°C.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retained at 45°C.
watch_item: The hybrid nanostructure may be challenging to fabricate with tight dimensional control and may introduce process variability at scale.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
